raw_response:
I'm sixty years old, been working this land since I was twenty. My old man taught me, and I've watched what works year after year. I finished middle school, so I can read a fertilizer bag and I went to a county training once about new wheat varieties, but honestly I trust my own eyes more than some expert from the city.

My place is 10.1 mu. It's just me and my wife now — the kids left for the city — so I have to think hard about labor. I split the land into two parts: 6 mu I keep for the wheat-maize rotation, and 4.1 mu I plant to cotton. The wheat and maize don't lie — they're my rice bowl. Cotton pays better when the price is right, but it needs hand-picking and lots of spraying, and at my age with only two of us, I can't handle too much of it.

**Wheat:** I plant winter wheat on those 6 mu every October. I use Jimai 22 — it's an improved variety, not hybrid, and I've used it for years. The neighbors switched to some new ones but I'm sticking with what I know. Last year I put down 40 jin per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, then topdressed twice with urea — about 20 jin total per mu. That works out to roughly 17 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze-up, once at jointing stage around Qingming, and once at grain filling. I spray pesticides three times — herbicide early, then fungicide and insecticide when I see problems. I rotary till before sowing. If the weather cooperates I expect about 500 kg per mu.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in early June, I plant summer maize on the same 6 mu. I buy Denghai 605 hybrid seed — it's what everyone around here uses, and it gives good yield. I don't till much after wheat, just plant straight into the stubble to save time before the rains come. I put down 25 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing, then topdress with urea at the big-trumpet stage — about 25 jin per mu total. That's about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, once at jointing and once at filling. Three pesticide sprays — herbicide, then insecticide for armyworm. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the summer storms don't flood me.

**Cotton:** On the 4.1 mu I plant Guoxin cotton in late April. I plough and rotary till in spring because cotton likes loose soil. I use about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu — cotton is a heavy feeder. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage. I spray pesticides 5 times through the season — bollworm is the enemy. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I know fertilizer costs are up this year, but I'd rather put on a bit too much than risk a bad harvest. A bad year means I eat into my savings. Wasting 50 yuan on extra urea is nothing compared to losing 500 jin of grain. I watch what my neighbors do — if Old Wang up the road is adding more topdressing, I pay attention. But mostly I do what I did last year, because change is risky and I've got only this one piece of land to feed us.
